decisions.statement: The editor calls one function to bring the panel up.
The fleet is read from the file the service writes rather than from the harness.
The panel draws the fleet that file has before any change to that file arrives.
The panel draws again when that file is written and at no other time.
An act on a seat asks for the file again rather than waiting to be told.
A row is spelled for the panel from the row the file has.
A color is carried on as its name.
The decoration reads that name.
One drawing runs at a time.
A state arriving mid-drawing is drawn once that drawing ends rather than dropped.
The rows go up before the terminals are swept.
A sweep that failed is said on the channel and leaves the rows drawn.
The badge counts the agents running and the description counts those agents again in words.
A filter narrowing the tree has its match count said against the running count.
A read that lost seats says the count lost rather than drawing a short tree in silence.
The terminal tabs with a seat are published after every drawing and on a tab change.
An act on a row is planned from that row's own state.
Copying a seat's name reaches the seat the same way an act does.
A stop on a subagent row is handed to `subagent-stopping` with the refresh.
No watcher on a seat file is registered here.
Nothing here hangs a row under another row or draws a row.
Nothing here knows the change a step makes to a seat.

definition: the fleet Alan watches, read from the file the service writes, and acted on
